column1: # The backtest panel: the repositories this reading is measured on, as opposed to the one it was
# developed against. One row per member, and the answer for each comes from outside this project.
# Columns: name, origin, sha, licence, domain, stated-by, arm
#   name        the directory the clone is expected under -Dcs.panel.dir
#   origin      the URL it is cloned from
#   sha         the commit it is pinned to. A reading of a moving target is not reproducible, and
#               every figure this library publishes is a reading of a named commit.
#   licence     Apache-2.0, MIT or BSD. Verified at the revision named above, not at HEAD.
#   domain      what the repository is about
#   stated-by   where that answer came from — the repository's own README one-liner, its GitHub
#               topics, its package description, or the standards body publishing its field. It is
#               recorded BEFORE the reading is run and never revised afterwards. An answer chosen
#               after reading the tree is the same defect as choosing OLiA after reading this one.
#   arm         in-domain | out-of-domain | no-taxonomy | degenerate
# Source: THIS PROJECT. That has to be said outright. Every other file bundled here is a curated
#   statement of a published standard, which is citable; this is a curated observation of a corpus,
#   which the doctrine refuses as evidence. IT IS A TEST FIXTURE AND IT NEVER VOTES. It is not on
#   the published classpath and nothing in the library reads it — only the panel diagnostic does.
# Licence: this file is part of this project and carries its licence. The repositories it names
#   carry their own, which is what the licence column is for.
# No member is named yet, and panelRead says so rather than reporting an empty result table as a
# result. What a member costs to add is: verify the licence at the revision, record the stated
# domain and who stated it, pin the SHA, and put it in an arm. Every domain needs at least one
# out-of-domain member, because a vocabulary that fires in its domain proves nothing until it is
# shown not to fire outside it, and the honest first result for those is silence.
